steps.candidate:
# Tier 1 — Project Memory

## Workflow
- Invoice fixtures under tests/fixtures/invoices/ are the ground truth for payload shapes [note 1].
- One route per resource; handlers stay thin, domain logic lives in src/domain/ [note 0].
- Imports are sorted alphabetically within each file and enforced by ESLint [note 1].

## Tech Stack
- Standardized on axios for outbound HTTP calls to support interceptors [note 2].
- Structured logging uses winston JSON lines to stdout, with one logger per module [note 5].
- Axios retries are logged at warn level via winston [note 5].

## Validation & Error Handling
- Zod v4.0.5 is the current validation library; schemas use `z.strictObject()` instead of `.strict()` [note 6].
- Zod v4 error utilities and issue list shape differ from v3; the error-mapper reads the v4 issue list [note 6].
- Express error handler returns 400 for validation failures and 500 otherwise [note 1].
- Credit-note payload schemas mirror invoice schemas and flatten cleanly in the error handler [note 4].

## Known pitfalls
- Prefer standard library functions over hand-rolled logic [note 2].
- Logging configuration must handle sensitive data redaction, but note that pino redaction paths are historical as the project migrated to winston [note 4].

## Task playbooks
- When upgrading Zod, update the error-mapper to handle the new issue list structure and replace `.strict()` with `z.strictObject()` [note 6].
- Configure winston loggers per module to maintain structured JSON output for the ops dashboard [note 5].

# Tier 1 — Project Memory

## Workflow
- Invoice fixtures under tests/fixtures/invoices/ are the ground truth for payload shapes [note 1].
- One route per resource; handlers stay thin, domain logic lives in src/domain/ [note 0].
- Imports are grouped by type (node builtins, external packages, internal aliases, relative paths); alphabetical sorting is retired [note 14].

## Tech Stack
- Outbound HTTP uses plain fetch; axios is forbidden [note 12].
- pino is the logging standard; winston was removed after data-loss incidents [note 13].
- pino redaction paths for sensitive data (e.g., card numbers) are active [note 13].

## Validation & Error Handling
- Zod v4.0.5 is the current validation library; schemas use `z.strictObject()` instead of `.strict()` [note 6].
- Zod v4 error utilities and issue list shape differ from v3; the error-mapper reads the v4 issue list [note 6].
- Express error handler returns 400 for validation failures and 500 otherwise [note 1].
- Credit-note payload schemas mirror invoice schemas and flatten cleanly in the error handler [note 4].
- Zod v4 validation covers query parameters, not just body payloads [note 11].

## Known pitfalls
- Prefer standard library functions over hand-rolled logic [note 2].
- pino async transports can drop logs under load; verify with soak tests [note 14].

## Task playbooks
- When upgrading Zod, update the error-mapper to handle the new issue list structure and replace `.strict()` with `z.strictObject()` [note 6].
- Configure pino loggers per module to maintain structured JSON output for the ops dashboard [note 13].
